item.title: SCP-5944: Re: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
Here are my thoughts on 5944;

Line by Line
Line by Line

openable only to on-site staff with Level 5 clearance or above

Very strange that only O5 council members can access the SCP's containment seeing how they generally aren't supposed to come in contact with anomalies.

SCP-5944 is a tactile cognitohazard in the form of an anomalous translucent crystal.

This sentence doesn't make sense to me. Is it a crystal with a cognitohazardous effect, because this sentence seems to imply that the crystal itself is like the physical embodiment of the cognitohazard or something?

General Thoughts
General Thoughts

The description is simply put, painful to get through. I'd say you could cut at least half of those words out and it'd still make just as much sense. There is no hook; some kind of mystery in the conprocs to pull you through all of that. By the second paragraph, I already understood what it was. None of the rest was necessary.

The anomaly itself is generic and boring. It's a crystal that turns people into zombies, and this skip does nothing interesting with it. The interview and experiment logs all blur together. It's just zombies being zombies. It's exactly what I expected based on the description. There is no twist or subversion. It doesn't lead anywhere. I suppose the final addendum is supposed to be some kind of conclusion but I honestly have no idea what it means.

I can't really suggest specific changes because I think the idea itself needs major reworking. I recommend checking out the Ideas Forum if you want some advice from experienced authors.

item.title: SCP-4712:
item.content:encoded:
My read-through of your series continues, finally.

Definitely enjoyed the structure here. Conceptually, there's little here to separate this from other extradimensional location type articles (4971 came to mind), but there's a sense of history and flow that I can appreciate regardless. I'm not a Sarkic person at all, so I was a bit in the dark about what's happening, but it was still readable. 4712-A is an interesting character and I wish he was expanded on in some way.

item.title: SCP-2684:
item.content:encoded:
I have had (though not in recent years) recurrent nightmares about the sea flooding the world. And perhaps not unlike the OP, I had an instance while playing in the sea and a big wave hit me. It couldt have carried me more than a foot ot two at the absolute outside (and only further up the beach in the direction I was looking), but the feeling of nearly being submerged and helplessness, momentary though it was, has stuck strongly with me to this day. So I totally grock that fear.

Have what, at time of posting, is your 100th upvote.

item.title: SCP-5991:
item.content:encoded: One of my favorite SCPs so far. It's a bit whacky but that's what makes it unique for me without stopping it from being creepy. As a newbie I wouldn't change anything except for one thing. Correct me if I'm wrong but, wouldn't SCP-5991-1's stomach be measured in km^3 instead of km^2 as it isn't a 2 dimensional plane?

item.title: LaRue Post - Willie's shine:
item.content:encoded: While I do agree with the points you laid out, I do feel as if focusing the story on the fight with the gator would pull the article away from its intended messege. This article is meant to be a small story that attempts to teach a simple leason. Be kind to your neihbors, and any details that didn't help push that lesson would feel ( to me at least ) superfluous. Also, on your point about the meanness feeling out of place. As someone who has lived in a small town in the south, while people tend to be friendlier, there is always gonna be asshole wherever you go. Especially if its a swamp full of outcasts and misfits.

item.title: SCP-5944: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
I can see this article is at about a 50/50 split right know between likes and dislikes. Judging the current trajectory, it'll probably slowly slip into the negatives. I know nobody is expected nor required to justify their votes, but I'd appreciate it if you could find the time to voice what didn't work for you, or what I could've done better.

This is my first SCP (and my first time writing fiction). I have a background in scientific writing, so I I didn't have too much trouble with the clinical tone. Is the narrative not strong enough? I really would like to improve and contribute something great to the site.

item.title: LaRue Post - Willie's shine:
item.content:encoded:
I find myself reading this and just…wishing it did more with the concept? There's a meanness the opening implies about La Rue that feels somewhat out of character for them, even if Joe did step in and prevent it; but equally the actual narrative feels…cliche and like we're seeing the cliff notes of a more interesting story; where all the actually engaging events are boiled down to a short mention.

My feeling is that this is somewhat caused by the actual GoI Format here: it doesn't provide a lot of room to do fun 'battles with a gator' moments or really in-depth characterisation or anything; but stuff like La Rue Posts - Brain Stew shows that it can work when you have some really evocative imagery in there and this…doesn't really?

item.title: SCP-5366:
item.content:encoded:
Erluzor’s dialogue is slightly distracting at times, making my suspension of disbelief waver, but Perl’s is so intensely ghostly that it brings be back in.

I really do like this. I was worried that this would be somewhat derivative of What Happens After, and while these elements are here, this story is wholly different. The concentration on a more grounded subject matter puts this in a unique perspective that I found interesting.
